text: `@Override` changes how a method is dispatched.
explanation: It has no members and `SOURCE` retention, so it is discarded before the class file exists — there is nothing left at run time to affect anything. Its entire effect is a rule in the compiler: if the marked method overrides nothing, report an error. Overriding happens whether you write it or not; what the annotation buys is turning Chapter 20's silent `equals(Point)` bug into a compile error.
